title: Patch-Diff and N-Day Variant Analyzer
goal: Analyze authorized patch diffs, advisories, and dependency changes to infer vulnerability root causes and search for safe variants in owned code.
scope: Repository integration, advisory intake, diff analysis, variant hypothesis generation, and tests for non-weaponized N-day analysis.
generation_reason: A major AI security capability is patch-diff reasoning: understanding what a patch fixed, where variants may exist, and what tests would prove exposure without publishing exploit details.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Analyze patches and generate defensive hypotheses only. Do not produce weaponized exploit chains.
constraints.authorized_code_only: Variant search must stay within authorized repositories, imported artifacts, or local fixtures.

success_criteria: The analyzer can ingest a patch diff or advisory reference and summarize likely bug class, affected preconditions, and defensive test ideas.
Variant hypotheses link to owned files/functions/routes/dependencies with evidence refs.
The system can create Codex build-lane tasks for tests or patches when exposure appears plausible.
Outputs avoid exploit weaponization and focus on detection, reproduction in local fixture, and remediation.
Tests prove unrelated code is marked not applicable or low-confidence instead of overclaiming exposure.

acceptance_criteria: Patch-diff analysis creates defensive hypotheses and test ideas without exploit weaponization.
Variant search is scoped to authorized code and records not-applicable decisions.
No live target execution or runtime mutation occurs.

before_promotion: NEXT_TASK.md must contain this task as the single active task.
after_completion: Promote the next true open task into NEXT_TASK.md, or record that no active backlog task remains in NEXT_TASK.md.
